# odyssey-058 review (Odyssey 12.101–191)

Reviewer, two full passes. Pass 1: every grammatical label, positional claim and cross-reference in every note,
checked against the line, `l`, `i` and the source text. Pass 2: Greek → `l` word by word, `l` ↔ `i`, remembered
English, quotation marks against 057 and the source line 12.192, and every parse in `gloss.json` (the 101 novel
forms and the 21 `__broaden__` entries (20 as drafted, one added)) against the line, plus a check of the known forms for uses the old entry
does not cover. `t` was not touched (verified unit by unit against the before-copy, and the joined `t` still
equals Murray 12.101–191). Line division of `l` equals that of `t` in every unit; no `\n` in any `i`; typographic
’ only; every repeated-line unit (111, 115, 142, 146, 147, 148–150, 152, plus 137/139/141 and 145/162 in part)
carries the published English. Murray prints no flagged scansion for this part (packet: none), so no unit needed
a metre sentence.

Counts: **1 major, 5 moderate, 11 minor** (16 edits; the six unaugmented-form parses are counted as one minor
item). 7 findings considered and refused (below).

Severity: major = a wrong fact or wrong quotation state that would ship; moderate = a false grammatical label,
false positional claim or missing/incorrect parse; minor = imprecise wording, ambiguous cross-reference, small
inconsistency between note and glossary.

νωιτέρην; ἐάᾳς/μέδηαι singular against ἵκοισθε plural. Quotation marks: Circe’s first speech opens in 057 (no mark
needed on unit 101) and closes at 110; Odysseus asks 112–114 (single unit, both marks); Circe answers 116–141 (opens
116, closes 141); Odysseus to his men 154–164 (opens 154, closes 164); the Sirens open at 184 (and now close at 191).
Repeated-line English identical to the published parts (the validator enforces whole units).

## Findings considered and refused

1. **Brief: “the Sirens’ speech at 12.184 runs into odyssey-059.”** Refused as a premise: 12.192 is the narrator
   (see the major change above). The speech is complete in this part.
2. **116–117 `l` “the works of war are a care / and toil”** can be read with “toil” as a second predicate noun.
   Refused: the Greek order (ἔργα μέμηλε καὶ πόνος) produces the same ambiguity, `l` follows the Greek order, and `i`
   and the note state the construction plainly.
3. **120 `i` “nor is there any might to oppose her”** supplies “to oppose her” not literally in οὐδέ τις ἔστ’ ἀλκή.
   Refused: ἀλκή is ‘strength to resist’, the supplied phrase is what the word means here, and `l` stays literal.
4. **107 `l` “he could not rescue you … not even the earth-shaker”** (“he” anticipating the late subject). Refused:
   a deliberate order-following device, and unambiguous with the apposition that follows.
5. **ἀνώγει / ἠνώγει “imperfect” in the 158 and 160 notes** (strictly a pluperfect-in-sense of ἄνωγα). Refused: the
   existing glossary entries and the house practice call them impf.; the notes agree with the glossary.
6. **ἐξίκετο, ἔντυνον: add “unaugmented”.** Refused: whether the epic form is augmented or unaugmented is not settled
   for these two (the stems begin with a vowel), and the runbook forbids claiming what cannot be checked.
7. **Existing glossary entries that look imprecise** (κιών “aor. part.” for a present participle; ὑπέκ “+ acc.”
   though it takes the genitive, already corrected by the broadening; ἵκοισθε “with κε” where this line has ἂν; δεινόν
   not flagged adverbial at 105). Not rewritten: “never rewrite an existing entry otherwise”; reported here for the
   owner. The 105 adverbial use is covered by “neut. nom./acc. sg.” and needs no new reading.

Also considered and left: 165 note “ἦ τοι is ‘so then’” against `l` “Indeed” (both legitimate renderings of ἦ τοι,
`i` “So”); 112 `i` “when she harms” for the optative in ὅτε σίνοιτο (acceptable at `i` level, `l` keeps “might”);
145 note could also cite 11.637 beside 9.178 (true but not needed).
